senses: as soon as (when followed by ubi, ut or quam)
la:adv:mox.html:
mox, adv.
etym. dub.; cf. Sanscr. mankshu, ready, soon
,
soon, anon, directly, presently; mostly of the future (class.).
Lit.
In gen.: mox ivero,: mox ego huc revertor,: jussit mihi nuntiari, mox se venturum,: mox tamen ardentīs accingar dicere pugnas Caesaris,; .—With quam: exspectant ... quam mox emittat currus, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 89 Vahl.); so, exspecto quam mox utatur,: quid exspectas quam mox ego dicam, etc.,: expectabant quam mox comitia edicerentur,; cf.: provisam quam mox vir meus redeat domum, Brix ad loc.: quam mox coctum est prandium?how soon,: mox ubi,as soon as,: mox ut, as soon as: mox ut caluere pugnā,: mox quam, as soon as (post-class.), .—
In partic.
Soon afterwards, thereupon, afterwards, then, in the next place: nam extemplo fusi, fugati: mox intra vallum compulsi: postremo exuuntur castris,: primum ... deinde ... mox ... post ... ; .—
Of a longer time, afterwards, at a later period (post - Aug. for post, postea): a quo mox principe Nero adoptatus est,; : ante hoc domūs pars videntur, mox reipublicae,: paulo mox,: paucis mox horis,.—
Transf., in the next place, then.
Of place and situation: ultra eos Dochi, deinde Gymnetes, mox Anderae,; cf.: pars equitum ... mox prima legio,. —
Of value, esteem: post amylum Chium maxime laudatur Creticum, mox Aegyptium,then,: tenuissimum camelis, mox equis,.
